elements.element: Preferred: no non-solicitation obligation binding Customer at all
elements.evidence: "Neither party shall, during such personnel's involvement with the Services and for 12 months after the end of that involvement, solicit for hire" — the restriction still binds the Customer (Company).

elements.element: Fallback: restriction is mutual (binds both parties equally)
elements.evidence: "Neither party shall..."; "This restriction is mutual, binding each party equally"

elements.element: Fallback: scope limited to personnel directly involved in the Services
elements.evidence: "any of the other party's personnel who have had direct involvement with the Services"; "applies only to personnel directly involved in the Services"
"for 12 months after the end of that involvement"

elements.element: Fallback: period runs from the end of that person's involvement (not from Agreement termination/term)
elements.evidence: "during such personnel's involvement with the Services and for 12 months after the end of that involvement" (replacing "during the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year after its termination")

elements.element: Fallback: carve-out for general advertisements not targeted at the other party's personnel
elements.evidence: "it does not restrict general advertisements not specifically targeted at the other party's personnel"

elements.element: Fallback: carve-out for unsolicited approaches by such personnel

elements.evidence: Only "solicit for hire as an employee, consultant or otherwise" is prohibited; no bar on hiring absent solicitation.

offending_extra_words: This restriction is mutual, binding each party equally, and applies only to personnel directly involved in the Services;
reasons: All atomic fallback elements are satisfied: mutuality, direct-involvement scope, 12 months measured per person from the end of that person's involvement, general-advertisement carve-out, unsolicited-approach carve-out, and no no-hire bar.
The preferred position (no non-solicit binding Customer) is not achieved, which is consistent with the drafter's locked fallback target.

Minimality falls slightly short: the added recital that the restriction "is mutual, binding each party equally, and applies only to personnel directly involved in the Services" duplicates protection already operative in the retained text ("Neither party shall" and "personnel who have had direct involvement with the Services"). Only the two carve-outs needed to be inserted.

Intent is preserved: the consent mechanic ("without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld") and all untouched terms remain effective; no undefined terms or dangling mechanics are introduced.
